name: Dusty Purple
lede: Dusty Purple is a muted, mid-dark [[purple]], carried by four separate sources on file, from the ISCC-NBS dictionary to a traditional Japanese name.

sections.title: One color, four records
sections.body:
The ISCC-NBS 1955 dictionary places this color in its crowded block 223, among more than fifty related names it calls "moderate purple", only 2.5 units away, one of the closest matches in our library [1]. Wikipedia, the 2010 xkcd survey and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary all separately carry versions of the same point [1][2]. In Munsell terms it reads about 6.9P 4.4/6.0 [1].

Our data also carries a traditional Japanese name at this color, *Hashita-iro*, written 半色 and meaning "half color", a shade once worn between the fully permitted and the restricted purples of the old court dress code [3]. Related names on file include [[dusty-lavender]], paler, and [[dull-purple]], its nearest named neighbor [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in only 3 of 23,781 paintings, one of the rarer matches among our color names, as photographed [4]. The clearest is Paul Signac's 1893 *[[painting:commons-Q17491415|Woman with a Parasol]]* [4]. In every match it plays the darkest shadow in its painting, never a mid-tone or a highlight [4]. Too few paintings share it to name a leading painter or decade with confidence [4]. These counts are a computed color match on photographs of aged, varnished paintings, not a pigment test [4].

origin.named_after: undocumented in Western sources; the Japanese Hashita-iro, 半色, "half color"
